nonblocking_findings: Possible slowdown on large streams: the filtered sequence `$leaves[not(f:is-head-note(.) and generate-id(f:head-note-div(.)) = $head-divs)]` is rebuilt for every leaf that reaches the `otherwise` branch of the `xsl:iterate` (reledmac.xslt:2617-2619). That is O(n²) calls to f:is-head-note per stream, and Saxon HE probably won't hoist it out of the loop. f:note-neighbor (4030-4031) also scans the whole sequence once per lookup. Output is correct either way. Suggested fix: compute the filtered sequence once as an `xsl:variable` next to `$head-divs`/`$notes-by-div` (2128-2145) and tunnel that variable. Before closure, compare the full mahzor build time against the old one.

Some leaves print nothing but still count as boundaries, because the skip list in f:note-neighbor (4039-4041) only covers whitespace text, empty tei:anchor, comments and PIs. Examples: an unrendered tei:milestone (2360-2371), a `parsha.*` milestone (2307-2316), and an echoed rubric (`@f:echoed='true'`, 3913), which is excluded as an instruction note. Two plain notes on either side of one of these sit at the same printed point but still get separate zero-width marks, so they can overlap. This errs on the safe side and is no worse than before, but it is a known remaining overlap. The PDF206 visual check has to confirm that none of these leaves sits between notes 128 and 129.

Mixed nesting falls back unevenly. When one note is a leaf and the next note is inside a leaf container (for example the last child of an inline j:conditional or seg that reaches the stream whole), the container counts as a boundary, so the two notes get separate marks at what may be the same printed point. Nothing breaks: the forward and backward lookups agree, so no mark is lost or printed twice. It is the old sibling-only behaviour, kept for nested notes.

Stream isolation looks correct. `$leaves` is local to each emit-leaves call, so the primary and alt streams of a parallel block never see each other's leaves. Nested contexts get no stream sequence: hoisted head notes set via the heading template, notes inside note content, and nested notes not in the sequence all use the sibling fallback, which is the old behaviour. Head notes are filtered out of the passed sequence, so a body note never merges with a hoisted note that is set elsewhere.

Note text and controls are kept. The diff only changes the text inside `\OSInterlinearNotemark{…}`. Every note still emits its own `\edtext`, `\Bfootnote`/`\Bendnote` choice (including the colophon rule), `\OSFootnotemark{serial}`, `\notenote` and note-content with direction handling. Instruction/description notes still end a group in both directions. Title-page notes use a separate template and are unaffected. The forward and backward lookups use the same sequence and the same skip predicate, so only the first note of a group prints the combined mark and the rest print an empty one. Marks are listed in the order the notes appear in the stream, which is also the order their apparatus entries are emitted, and each mark uses f:note-mark, so the numbering style is unchanged.

Missing test coverage (not blocking): (a) no parallel/reledpar regression, although the QA blocker is on parallel page PDF206; (b) no test that a hoisted head note next to a body note in the stream does not merge with it; (c) no explicit test that an anchor with content stays a boundary; (d) no test of the nested sibling fallback (a note inside an inline container next to a note that is a leaf). The new wrapper test does cover skipping an empty tei:anchor across a wrapper and a transclusion, and the paragraph test covers paragraph separation. Adding (a) and (b) is recommended.
verdict: Approve the code change. The new helper correctly finds neighbouring notes in the order one stream prints its leaves, falls back to XML siblings for nested notes, keeps paragraphs, rubrics, columns and parallel blocks as boundaries, and keeps every apparatus entry and its controls. Nothing blocks. Before this is final, hoist the per-leaf filter out of the loop and add parallel and hoisted-note regression tests. This review does not approve the rendered page: the rebuilt PDF206 page still needs its separate visual check, which must confirm that notes 128 and 129 now print as one comma-separated mark and that no silent boundary leaf (an unrendered milestone or echoed rubric) sits between them.
